title: Building City-Scale Vision AI Systems in New Zealand
location: WG Building 2 Governor Fitzroy Place, Auckland Central, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
**嘉宾介绍 \| Guest Speaker**
**Derek Zhang**
Dr. Derek Zhang 是 Auckland Transport 的 Computer Vision Delivery Manager，负责领导 Vision AI 解决方案在城市交通网络中的设计、开发与落地。他拥有 Computer Vision 博士学位，从零构建了 AT 的 in-house 计算机视觉能力，打造了可扩展的 CV 平台与应用，有效提升了交通安全、运营效率以及数据驱动决策能力。
Derek 擅长将前沿的 Vision AI 技术转化为企业级的实际应用成果，同时注重打造高绩效团队，并推动跨团队与 stakeholder 的紧密协作。

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**主题 \| Topic**

本次分享将探讨 Computer Vision 如何从实验性的 AI 技术，逐步发展为现代城市中的关键基础设施。基于在 Auckland Transport 的真实实践经验，Dr. Derek Zhang 将介绍 Vision AI 系统是如何被设计、部署并扩展，以支撑城市级交通网络运行。

内容将从通俗易懂的角度介绍 Computer Vision 的基本概念及工作原理，并结合实际案例（如 incident detection、traffic monitoring、safety analytics），展示如何将视频数据转化为可执行的洞察，从而提升城市运行效率与安全性。
此外，分享还将深入讲解这些系统背后的构建方式，包括实时平台、数据管道、系统运维，以及隐私与公众信任等关键考虑。
最后，Derek 将结合实践总结关键经验，并分享在构建 in-house 能力和实现 AI 规模化落地过程中的领导力思考与职业发展建议。

title: Ngā Whetū o te Tau Hou | The Stars of the New Year
location: Te Whatu Stardome | Observatory & Planetarium, 670 Manukau Rd, Maungakiekie/One Tree Hill Domain, Epsom, Auckland 1023, Auckland
description:
In this immersive planetarium experience, you’ll journey through the night sky to explore the Matariki star cluster and its importance in Aotearoa and te ao Māori.
Discover the rich pūrākau (stories), science and traditions connected to each of the nine whetū, learn about the Maramataka (the Māori lunar calendar), and reflect on how Matariki guides us through the cycles of the year along with many other significant stars.
Whether you’re reconnecting with Matariki or experiencing it for the first time, this show is a great way to honour the season and gain a deeper appreciation of Māori astronomy and our place within the cosmos.
Keywords: Nga Whetu o te Tau Hou The Stars of the New Year

title: Community planting days - Hibiscus Coast
location: Okoromai-Clansman Reserve, Army Bay, 9 Okoromai Views, Gulf Harbour. Auckland, Auckland
description:
Join Restore Hibiscus & Bays for our 2026 community planting days across the Hibiscus Coast.
From May through to August we have planting days happening at reserves across Red Beach, Gulf Harbour, Silverdale, Orewa, Army Bay, Whangaparāoa and Hatfields Beach - including a special Matariki celebration planting in July.
What is it? 
A community planting day where volunteers come together to plant native trees in local reserves. Every tree planted creates vital habitat for wildlife, stabilises coastal and stream edges, and enhances the natural beauty of the Hibiscus Coast for generations to come.
Who can come? 
Everyone is welcome - individuals, families, businesses and community groups of all ages and backgrounds. No experience needed.
What's involved? 
You'll be planting native trees and shrubs under the guidance of our team. Events run for 2-4 hours depending on the site. It's outdoors, active, and a great way to meet your neighbours and give back to your local environment.
What to bring:

Gardening gloves
A clean spade (if you have one - tools provided if not)
Water and snacks
Sturdy closed-toe shoes
Warm layers - it's winter!
Gumboots are recommended for Wetland planting days.

What's provided:

All tools and equipment
Native plants
Guidance and instruction throughout.

Group and corporate planting day bookings are also available, contact info@restorehb.org.nz to find out more.
For full event dates, locations, and to find your nearest planting day visit the Restore website.

title: OWASP New Zealand - Auckland Meetup
description:
Join us for the next **OWASP New Zealand Chapter** meetup! We are gathering the local application security community for an evening of technical talks, networking, and knowledge sharing.

* **When:** Tuesday, 14th July 2026
* **Where:** **Lightspeed Office** 2 Nuffield Street, Newmarket, Auckland 1023, New Zealand
* **Time:** 5:30 PM (Doors open for networking), 6:00 PM (Presentations begin)

We present an introductory talk about the OWASP Top 10 (2025 edition) with a new item each meeting. With the new edition OWASP Top 10, we're starting at A01:2025 Broken Access Control.

**Thanks to Our Host**
A big thank you to [Lightspeed](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/au/) for sponsoring the venue and catering and for supporting the local security community.

**Agenda**

* 6:00 PM OWASP Introduction, Top 10
* 6:30 PM Break
* 6:45 PM Technical Talk

**Technical Topic Speaker: Ricky Gummadi**
Ricky Gummadi is a Senior Solution Architect at Microsoft, based in Auckland, focused on AI, cloud architecture, and developer platforms. He works closely with enterprise customers across New Zealand to design and implement production-ready AI systems. Ricky is also part of the core development team contributing to the Agent Governance Toolkit, with a focus on enabling safe, reliable, and governed agentic AI workloads.
**Talk Title: Agentic AI Governance**
As AI systems evolve from assistants to autonomous agents, the focus shifts from what the model says to what the system actually does. This talk introduces the Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT), a framework for bringing deterministic, runtime governance to agentic systems. We’ll explore why prompt-based safety is not sufficient for production scenarios, walk through the OWASP Agentic Top 10 risks, and look at how policies, identity, sandboxing, and observability can be applied to mitigate these risks in real-world architectures.

title: The Beginner's Guide to Stoicism
location: 37 Normanby Road, Mount Eden, Auckland 1024, Auckland
description:
A discussion around what Stoicism is, where it came from, and then a look into the virtues, principles, and finally, how to put Stoicism into our daily lives. Come and join us for a philosophical discussion

**What is Stoicism?**
Stoicism is an ancient Greek philosophy that teaches you how to remain calm under pressure, think clearly in chaos, and focus on what you can actually control. It is a practical, action‑focused philosophy.
Stoicism is **not** about suppressing emotions or becoming cold. It’s about responding to life’s challenges with wisdom and inner strength rather than impulse and reactivity.
**Core ideas:**

1. **Focus on what you control:** your thoughts, choices, efforts, and responses
2. **Accept what you don’t control:** other people’s behaviour, outcomes, circumstances, the past
3. **Live according to virtue:** wisdom, courage, justice, and temperance

**Origins**
Stoicism began around **300 BCE**. After being shipwrecked near Athens, **Zeno of Citium** discovered a book about Socrates that changed the course of his life. He spent years studying with the city’s leading philosophers and eventually developed his own distinctive system.
Zeno taught at the **Stoa Poikile** (“Painted Porch”), a public colonnade decorated with murals. The philosophy takes its name from this place — **Stoicism**.
**Famous Stoics:**

* **Marcus Aurelius** – Roman Emperor
* **Seneca** – Roman Senator and playwright
* **Epictetus** – Former slave turned influential teacher

**The Four Virtues**
The Stoics believed a good life is built on four cardinal virtues:

* **Wisdom** — understanding what is good, bad, and indifferent
* **Courage** — acting rightly despite fear or difficulty
* **Justice** — treating others fairly and fulfilling your social role
* **Temperance** — exercising self‑control, moderation, and balance

**Key Principles**
**The Dichotomy of Control** Everything in life falls into two categories:
**Within Our Control:**

* Our thoughts and judgments
* Our action

title: LIVE Day: Weather Science
location: MOTAT, 805 Great North Road and 98 Motions Road, Western Springs, Auckland, Auckland
description:
LIVE Days are interactive and hands-on days filled with learning, play and special moments, perfect for the whole whānau!
With live entertainment, collection items, plus plenty of activities - there's a little something for everyone.
This July at LIVE DAY: Weather Science uncover the stories of the weather-related stars in the Matariki cluster, Waipunarangi and Ururangi.
Waipunarangi is associated with the various forms of rain that we experience throughout the year as it falls from the sky and washes over the earth, nourishing all living things. If you can’t see Waipunarangi clearly during Matariki, the year will bring lots of rain and maybe some flooding. If she’s bright and clear, the rain will be light.
Ururangi connects us to the different winds and this whetū determines the nature of these winds. If Ururangi is hard to see when the cluster of Matariki rises, the year will be windy. If he is bright and clear, the winds will be calm.
Make and take home your own cloud finder, have fun with weather science experiments featuring raindrops and rainbows, and find out more about the different winds and how they work at our latest exhibition Ngā hau a Tāwhirirangi Forces of Flight, in the Aviation Hall.
Included in General Admission.
We recommend parking outside the Aviation Hall and enjoying the free heritage tram ride between sites.

title: Papa Ki Awataha Planting Day
description:
Come along for a rewarding day of planting at Papa ki Awataha, the source of Northcote’s treasured greenway.
Together we’ll enhance this important urban ecosystem by planting native species along the stream banks and nearby reserves.
Make a day of it by exploring the nearby playgrounds and green spaces afterwards or enjoy a bite at one of Northcote’s many local eateries. Sign up and bring your whānau and friends!
Planting is a powerful way to honour Matariki. By getting your hands dirty at Papa ki Awataha, you’ll help restore the mauri of this special place.
Your efforts will support native biodiversity, stabilise stream banks, create habitat, and contribute to long-term carbon capture. This is your chance to give back to te taiao and leave a living legacy in your community.

Responding to Hiwa-i-te-rangi, the Matariki star of hopes and aspirations, artists will explore tūmanako (hopes), wawata (dreams), whakapapa (genealogy) and kaitiakitanga (guardianship of the environment).

title: Whiria te Tāngata
location: Nathan Homestead Pukepuke, 70 Hill Road, Manurewa, Auckland 2102, Auckland
description:
Join us over the Matariki period for this exhibition, workshops and other activities centred on the art of raranga techniques, both in traditional harakeke and other materials.
Jane Wilks (Ngāti Tauaiti, Ngai te Rangi) will present pieces which use traditional materials alongside wire and synthetic textiles, and sometimes in forms which comment on colonial influences on Te Ao Māori. Jane Wilks’s work is grounded in our connections with the natural world. Each piece examines a different facet of this kaupapa.
Tania Mae Miller (Te Ngahengahe, Nga Puhi) will showcase a large variety of Mahi Raranga woven from (Phormium tenax), Muka (Harakeke fibre) and Kiekie (Freycinetia banksia). These works are manifested through the concepts of Whakapapa and Whanaungatanga.
Waiata Ngataki (Wakahuia Kaiwhakahaere for Ngāti Tamaoho Trust) will be present on the practice and use of raranga as a taonga in everyday life and ceremonial contexts.

Expect big energy, big characters and a room full of hype as dancers showcase their individuality, storytelling and connection to the music.
Whether you’re battling, spectating or cheering from the sidelines, this is one of the most joyful and expressive dance events of the year!
Proudly supported by Creative New Zealand and Corban Estate Arts Centre.

title: Caluzzi Cabaret's 30th Birthday
location: The Civic, Corner of Queen Street and 269-287 Wellesley Street West, Auckland City Centre, Auckland
description:
Thirty years of laughter, lashes and larger-than-life drag unleashed!
Karangahape Road’s brightest stars are hitting the stage in a once-in-a-generation celebration.
Caluzzi Cabaret, Australasia’s longest-running drag cabaret, marks its 30th anniversary with a dazzling new showcase created exclusively for the Auckland Live Cabaret Festival.
Fronted by internationally loved queens, Caluzzi owners and TV personalities Kita Mean and Anita Wigl’it (Drag Wars, House of Drag, RuPaul’s Drag Race Down Under), the show explodes with high-camp glamour, whip-smart comedy and jaw-dropping production numbers that capture the heart and legacy of NZ’s iconic Caluzzi Cabaret.
Plus, legendary cast member Ling Ling and her girls join the celebrations adorned in feathers, rhinestones and mischief.
This is Caluzzi - bigger, bolder and more fabulous than ever.
Happy Birthday Caluzzi - let us eat cake!

title: Gil Shaham Plays Beethoven
location: Auckland Town Hall, 301-317 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre 1010, Auckland
description:
Conductor Antony HermusViolin Gil Shaham
Beethoven Violin ConcertoProkofiev Cinderella (selections)
Beethoven’s towering concerto stands in Olympian solitude. Its technical challenges test the strongest violinists; its artistic ones expose the soul of the supreme musicians. Gil Shaham, appearing for the first time in New Zealand, is unquestionably such an artist.
Prokofiev saw the heroine of his ballet as more than a fairytale character, calling her ‘a real person, feeling, experiencing, and moving among us’. He clothes her in music which, by turns, is sprightly, ebullient, and sweetly full of heartfelt longing.
